n: Thirteen years after Ishmael’s birth, the Lord appears to Abram, now ninety-nine. God reveals Himself as “the Almighty” and calls Abram to live faithfully in His presence and be whole-hearted.

f.g: Hebrew El Shaddai, a name of God emphasizing His power and sufficiency.

n: God promises to confirm His covenant and greatly multiply Abram’s family.
Abram falls on his face in reverence, a natural response to God’s holy presence.

f.g: Bowed to the ground in worship.

n: God declares that Abram will be the father of many nations. The covenant reaches far beyond one people.
God renames Abram to Abraham. A new name marks a new identity and covenant relationship—a pattern found in baptism, the temple, and taking Christ’s name upon us.

f.g: Abram means “exalted father”; Abraham is explained as “father of a multitude.”

n: Nations and kings will come from Abraham—fulfilled through Israel’s kings, including David, and ultimately the King of kings, Jesus Christ.

f.w: kings shall come out of thee

n: The heart of the covenant: God will be their God forever. Latter-day Saints understand this as the everlasting covenant of the gospel, renewed in our day.

f.w: to be a God unto thee

n: God promises the land of Canaan as an everlasting possession, though Abraham still lives there as a foreigner.

f.g: A resident foreigner without property rights.

n: Abraham and his descendants have their part: to keep the covenant. Covenants involve promises on both sides.
Circumcision is given as the sign of the covenant for every male. This physical mark would remind God’s people that they belonged to Him.

f.g: Removal of the foreskin; for Israel, the outward sign of covenant membership.

n: Circumcision is a “token,” a sign. The JST explains it was given partly because people had strayed from correct ordinances, including baptism.

f.g: JST Genesis 17:3-7 says people had departed from God’s ordinances and the baptism He commanded.

n: Boys are to be circumcised at eight days old, including servants born in the household or purchased. The JST connects the eighth day with the teaching that children become accountable at eight years.

f.g: JST Genesis 17:11-12 links this to children not being accountable until eight years old.

n: The covenant is to be “in your flesh,” a permanent reminder. Scripture later teaches that true circumcision is of the heart.

f.w: my covenant shall be in your flesh

n: Refusing circumcision means breaking the covenant and being cut off from God’s people. To reject the sign is to reject the relationship.
Sarai also receives a new name: Sarah. She is fully part of the covenant, not just Abraham’s companion.

f.g: Both Sarai and Sarah are forms meaning “princess.”

n: God promises to bless Sarah personally and give her a son. She will be mother of nations and kings.
Abraham bows and laughs. His laughter may mix joy and disbelief at the thought of a 100-year-old father and 90-year-old mother. The name Isaac will come from this laughter.

f.g: Hebrew tsaḥaq, the root of Isaac’s name.

n: Abraham pleads for Ishmael, the son he already loves. It is a father’s prayer.

f.w: O that Ishmael might live before thee!

n: God insists: Sarah will bear a son, named Isaac, and the covenant will continue through him.
God answers Abraham’s prayer for Ishmael too. Ishmael will be blessed with many descendants and twelve princes—a great nation.

f.g: A wordplay on Ishmael’s name, “God hears.”

n: The covenant line, however, will run through Isaac, born to Sarah within a year.

f.w: at this set time in the next year

n: God finishes speaking and departs, “going up” from Abraham, suggesting a personal appearance.
That very day, Abraham obeys completely, circumcising every male in his household. His obedience is immediate.
Abraham is ninety-nine when he is circumcised—an old man entering a new covenant sign.
Ishmael is thirteen. Many Arab peoples later traditionally practiced circumcision around this age.

f.g: Ishmael too receives the covenant sign, though the covenant line will pass through Isaac.

n: Father and son are circumcised on the same day, sharing the covenant sign together.

f.g: Repeated to stress Abraham’s prompt obedience.

n: All the men of the household, including servants and foreigners, are circumcised. From the start, outsiders could join the covenant family.

f.w: bought with money of the stranger
